Author: Harish Kumar

 Versus
 1. The State of Bihar
 2. Kajal Kumari @ Kajal Thakur D/o Naveen Thakur R/O Village- Purani
 Dudari, Ward No.- 09, P.S- Bettiah Town (Kalibag Op), Distt.- West
 Champaran.

 Appearance :
 For the Petitioner/s : Mr. Jitendra Kumar, Adv.
 For the Opposite Party/s : Mr. Rana Randhir Singh, App
 For the O.P. No.2 : Mr. Sashank Shekhar, Adv.
 ======================================================
 Coram: Honourable Mr. Justice Harish Kumar
 Oral Order
3 13-12-2023
Heard Mr. Jitendra Kumar, learned counsel for the petitioner and learned APP for the State.

O.P.
No.2 is represented by Mr. Sashank Shekhar.

2. The petitioner, who happens to be husband of the complainant (O.P. No.2) is apprehending his arrest in connection with Complaint Case No. 1157(C) of 2020, wherein cognizance has been taken for the offences under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code and Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
3. The marriage of the petitioner was solemnized with the complainant (O.P. No.2) in the year 2017.

However, soon Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.57879 of 2023(3) dt.13-12-2023 after the marriage,
she was allegedly subjected to demand of dowry and on non-fulfillment of the same, she was tortured in various ways and finally ousted from her matrimonial home resulting into filing of the present complaint case.

The couple also blessed with a female child, who is at present living with the Pankaj Kumar @ Pankaj Thakur vs The State Of Bihar on 13 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137781292/
1 O.P. No.2.
4.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that admittedly the marriage of the petitioner was solemnized in the year 2017, and as such, at this belated stage, any demand of dowry and cruelty,
does not inspire confidence.

That apart, the solemn affirmation of the complainant has also been recorded, wherein she has categorically stated that she is working as a Tutor in a school at Muzaffarpur, where her husband used to visit time and again.
Learned counsel for the petitioner further submits that the petitioner is still ready to keep O.P. No.2, as his wife with full honour and dignity 5.
On the other hand, learned counsel for O.P. No.2, submits that because of the ill behavior of the petitioner to such an extent that it is not possible for O.P. No.2 to live with him.
However, if there is any chance of one time settlement, O.P. No.2, is also willing to settle the matter.

6. Considering the submissions made on behalf of the Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.57879 of 2023(3) dt.13-12-2023 parties, let the matter be relegated to the Patna High Court Mediation &
Conciliation Centre.
The parties are directed to appear before the learned Mediator on 19.01.2024 along with the relevant documents, wherein the learned Mediator shall take all the endeavours to resolve the disputes.

7. Re-notify this case on 07.02.2024 along with the report of the Mediation and Conciliation Centre.
8.
In the meantime, no coercive steps shall be taken against the petitioner in connection with Complaint Case No. 1157(C) of 2020, till further order.

(Harish Kumar, J) rohit/-
